segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now the apostles and the brothers and sisters who were throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles too had received the word of God.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision took issue with him,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “You went into the house of uncircumcised men and ate with them!”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Peter began and laid it all out for them in order, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: an object like a large sheet coming down, lowered from heaven by its four corners, and it came right up to me.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: I looked at it closely and studied it, and I saw the four-footed animals of the earth, the wild beasts, the crawling things, and the birds of the sky.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: I also heard a voice saying to me, ‘Get up, Peter; slaughter and eat.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But I said, ‘Certainly not, Lord, for nothing profane or unclean has ever entered my mouth.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: But a voice answered a second time from heaven, ‘What God has made clean, you must not call profane.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: This happened three times, and then everything was drawn up again into heaven.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And right at that moment three men, sent to me from Caesarea, arrived at the house where we were.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: The Spirit told me to go with them, making no distinction. These six brothers also came with me, and we entered the man’s house.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: He reported to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, ‘Send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter;

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: he will speak words to you by which you will be saved, you and your whole household.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, just as on us at the beginning.

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: And I remembered the Lord’s words, how he said, ‘John baptized with water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: So if God gave them the same gift he gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I to be able to stand in God’s way?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When they heard this, they fell silent, and they glorified God, saying,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “So then, God has granted even the Gentiles the repentance that leads to life.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Now those who had been scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen travelled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who came to Antioch and began speaking to the Greek speakers as well, announcing the good news of the Lord Jesus.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number who believed turned to the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: The report about them reached the ears of the church in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas out as far as Antioch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: When he arrived and saw the grace of God, he was glad, and he urged them all to hold fast to the Lord with resolute hearts,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And a considerable crowd was added to the Lord.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he went off to Tarsus to look for Saul,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. And it came about that for a whole year they met together with the church and taught a considerable crowd, and that the disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: One of them, named Agabus, stood up and made known through the Spirit that a great famine was about to come over the whole inhabited world; this took place under Claudius.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: So the disciples decided, each as their means allowed, to send aid to the brothers and sisters living in Judea.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: This they did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.

notes.note: The Greek plural was the ordinary way to address or describe a mixed group of men and women, here the community of believers. “Brothers and sisters” gives what a first-century reader would have understood. In verse 12, where six particular companions of Peter are meant, “brothers” is kept.

notes.traditional: they that were of the circumcision
notes.note: The phrase can simply mean Jewish believers, which at this point would be nearly the whole Jerusalem community. It can also mean a narrower group within it that insisted on circumcision for Gentile converts. Scholars are divided, and the literal rendering leaves both readings open.

The Greek word ordinarily means “shared” or “ordinary,” but in Jewish usage it had come to describe what is not set apart as holy and is therefore ritually defiling. “Common” no longer conveys this to a modern reader, and some versions use “impure.” “Profane” keeps the contrast with what is holy, and the related verb in verse 9 is rendered “call profane” to preserve the echo.
Many manuscripts read “where I was,” and older English versions follow them. The reading “we were,” found in early witnesses, is printed in SBLGNT and translated here.

The verb here is active and most naturally means “making no distinction,” that is, between Jew and Gentile. Some take it like the middle form in the parallel at 10:20, “without hesitating,” and the manuscripts vary in the form of the word. The same verb is used in verse 2 of those who “took issue” with Peter, an echo English cannot easily reproduce.

The participle “having believed” may attach to “us” (the gift came to us when we believed), to “them,” or to both groups. The translation takes it with “us,” the nearest word, as most versions do. On any reading, the gift is tied to trust in the Lord Jesus Christ and not to circumcision.

Manuscripts are divided between Hellenistas (“Greek speakers,” the word used of Greek-speaking Jews in 6:1) and Hellenas (“Greeks”). SBLGNT prints the former, which is translated here. Whichever word is original, the contrast with “Jews” in verse 19 shows that non-Jews are meant, and most scholars agree on that sense.

The word is formed with a Latin-style ending used for the adherents or partisans of a leader, so it means roughly “Christ’s people.” It was most likely coined by outsiders in Antioch rather than by the believers, who in Acts call themselves disciples, brothers, or followers of the Way. The term occurs only three times in the New Testament.

The Greek term means the inhabited world, and in ordinary usage of the period it was in practice the Roman world. Claudius was emperor from AD 41 to 54, and his reign saw repeated food shortages in various regions. Josephus records a severe famine in Judea in the mid-to-late 40s.

candidates.reason: Occurs throughout Acts and the letters; “church,” “assembly” and “congregation” are all defensible and the choice must be uniform.
The plural for the believing community recurs in nearly every book, and translators differ between “brothers” and “brothers and sisters.”
The plural alternates between “Gentiles” and “nations” across the New Testament and needs a rule for when each applies.
“Repentance” is traditional, but the word’s sense of a change of mind or turning is rendered variously and should be decided once.
The ritual sense (with the verb κοινόω) recurs in Mark 7, Acts 10–11, Romans 14 and Hebrews, where versions vary between “common,” “impure,” “profane” and “defiled.”
